title: Priority Lane Framework for Cross-Customer Commitment Requests with Revenue Attribution
creator: Anika Bose
description: Problem statement: We get a high volume of non-bug enterprise requests related to commitments, invoicing exceptions, and marketplace offsets. Current routing is ad-hoc (email + Slack) and frequently causes: delayed decisions, inaccurate revenue attribution, and missed SLA expectations for finance and sales. Goal: define an intake + prioritization framework that (1) routes each request to an appropriate lane (self-serve / sales-assisted / enterprise-handshake), (2) attaches a clear revenue attribution and cost-allocation recommendation, and (3) provides a near-real-time dashboard for PM, Sales Ops, and Finance.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight scoring engine in the intake form that computes a Priority Score based on: ARR impact, requested SLA change, legal/finance complexity, marketplace offset presence, and engineering effort estimate. Scores map to three lanes with clear SLAs and templated next steps. Implement an initial manual review step for 'enterprise-handshake' lane then iterate to automate routing rules for repeatable patterns. Integrate outputs with CRM (Zendesk/Salesforce) and internal billing spreadsheet for auditability.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Speed vs fidelity: a coarse scoring model enables fast routing but will surface more false positives; a high-fidelity model requires more fields and slows intake.
Manual reviews vs automation: manual review provides safety for high-dollar deals but increases Ops workload; automation needs historical data and iterative tuning.
Revenue recognition risk: certain marketplace offsets require finance sign-off before approval to avoid revenue leakage.
Customer experience: over-automation risks frustrating customers who expect human touch for complex billing asks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake form template created and published (Confluence + Drive) with required fields listed.
A2: Scoring logic implemented as a simple spreadsheet prototype and validated against 20 historical requests (baseline accuracy >= 80% for lane assignment).
A3: Three routing lanes defined with SLA targets: Self-serve (48h), Sales-assisted (5 business days), Enterprise-handshake (10 business days).
A4: Notification workflow built (Slack + email) for assigned owners and Sales Ops.
A5: Dashboard wireframe available in Console for PM/Finance showing queue, predicted ARR impact, and decision timestamps.
A6: Hand-off checklist for finance/legal created; at least one pilot customer run completed.
A7: Integration point documented for CRM with a sample webhook payload and owners identified.
